cohort: 136,098 singleton birth infants born between 1995 and 2003 in the PRIMA (Prevention of RSV: Impact on Morbidity and Asthma) cohort
finding: Early-life exposures, including maternal UTI during pregnancy, mode of delivery, infant antibiotic use, and having older siblings at home, were associated with an increased risk of childhood asthma in a cumulative and dose-dependent manner.
mod_finding: Compared with vaginal delivery, C-section delivery increased odds of childhood asthma by 34% in the univariate analysis and 11% after adjusting for other environmental exposures and covariates.
